subject: POC Success Criteria & KPIs — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria / next steps

Alex — great conversation earlier. Thanks for walking us through Atlas Payments' primary goals and constraints. As discussed, below is a draft of the POC success criteria and proposed KPIs we can use to evaluate Redwood in the trial environment. Please review and flag anything missing or unrealistic.

Goals (high level)
- Validate inference performance for customer-facing payment flows (latency and throughput)
- Confirm cost/run-rate estimates under typical traffic profiles
- Validate output quality on real prompts (match to existing rules + reduction in false positives)
- Verify integration & security posture for a production pilot

Proposed POC success criteria (must-haves)
1) Latency: p95 end-to-end inference <= 150 ms for standard auth flow (typical prompt size ~200 tokens).
2) Throughput: sustain 50 req/s with 99% of requests completed within SLO window during burst tests.
3) Cost: amortized cost <= $0.0008 per token (model + infra) at expected batch sizes.
4) Quality: automated accuracy >= 92% on the provided test set (we'll run a 300-sample set plus 50 edge cases); no regression on top-5 rules.
5) Reliability: no more than 0.5% error rate under 24h soak with realistic traffic mix.

Ownership & timeline
- Redwood: provisioning, baseline performance tests, and providing an MOP + ingestion instructions (Marissa will lead).
- Atlas: provide sample prompt set, acceptance criteria, and a procurement contact for the trial contract (Samir / procurement).
- Proposed timeline:
  - Kickoff & environment setup: Week 1 (this week)
  - Baseline tests & initial tuning: Week 2
  - Customer evaluation & quality checks: Week 3
  - Final review & decision: Week 4

Next steps (action items)
- I will send the MOP + list of artifacts we need (access, sample prompts, expected traffic pattern). Attachment: redwood_poc_mop_v1.pdf
- Alex / Samir: confirm the sample set owner and targeted date to share it.
- Marissa: once we have the sample prompts, can you run a baseline with existing configs and share the latency samples?

If this looks reasonable I’ll schedule a 30-minute kick-off for early next week to align teams.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@atlas-payments.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC success criteria / next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This reads well and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications:

- Latency: 150 ms p95 is our current target, but for the auth flow anything under 200ms p95 would be acceptable for the POC as long as the production plan shows improvement paths.
- Throughput: 50 req/s is correct for peak. We’ll also want a shorter burst test at 200 req/s for 2 minutes to validate autoscaling behavior.
- Cost: your target looks reasonable; we’ll compare against our current provider numbers. Please include cost breakdown assumptions (tokens per call, batch size) in the MOP.
- Quality: we’ll own labeling for the 300-sample set. I’ll have an engineer pick a representative set by Friday.

Logistics: Samir will coordinate procurement for a short trial agreement and provide a PO if needed. Procurement is looped in.

We can do kickoff Monday (7/5) 10am ET — Samir, does that work?

Best,
Alex Tan
Director, Product
Atlas Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Alex Tan <alex.tan@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria / next steps

Thanks Jordan — I'll take point on the baseline tests. Couple of technical notes / asks:

- Please provide the representative prompt set and indicate expected token counts per call (we need distributions to choose batch sizes).
- For throughput tests we'll run two profiles: steady-state @50 req/s for 30 minutes, and burst test @200 req/s for 2 minutes. We'll record p50/p95/p99 and error rate.
- We will include KV cache warmup in the baseline run to reflect real traffic; please indicate any session affinity requirements.
- Security checklist: please confirm whether Atlas wants logs masked at token-level and if there are retention requirements (we will provide SOC2 artifacts if needed).

I’m attaching a CSV with the initial latency sample schema we’ll return (baseline_latency_samples.csv). Once we have the sample prompts we’ll run an initial pass and share the results by Friday EOD.

-Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlas-payments.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria / next steps (procurement/terms)

Hi all — looping in on procurement and minimal terms. Quick items from our side:

- Trial agreement: we can issue a 30-day evaluation agreement covering usage and standard data processing terms. If Atlas needs a Mutual NDA or custom SLA, please indicate and we’ll route to legal.
- PO: If Atlas will issue a PO for the trial, please include the Deal ID (DEAL-8421) and confirm billing contact.
- Data handling: Redwood collects logs to troubleshoot the POC; we can agree to a 30-day log retention and provide filtered logs (masking PII). If Atlas requires longer retention or specific controls (KMS/HSM), we’ll need to scope that separately.

Samir / procurement: can you confirm whether you prefer Redwood’s eval agreement or a short form PO? We can turn the eval agreement around within 1 business day once we have the contact.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@atlas-payments.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria / next steps — confirmed items and kickoff

Alex / Samir — thanks for the quick responses. Confirming agreed items and next steps so we’re aligned before the kickoff: 

Agreed success criteria (finalized)
- Latency: target p95 <= 200 ms for the POC (goal 150 ms p95 for production planning)
- Throughput: steady-state 50 req/s; burst 200 req/s for 2 minutes
- Cost: baseline target <= $0.0008/token; Redwood to provide cost assumptions and batch-size sensitivity
- Quality: >= 92% on Atlas-labeled 300-sample set; Redwood to run initial inference and provide labeled outputs for Atlas review
- Reliability: error rate <= 0.5% during 24h soak test

Action items / owners
- Atlas: share sample prompt set + token distribution by EOD Friday (Samir / Alex)
- Redwood (Marissa): run baseline tests and return baseline_latency_samples.csv and a short report by Friday EOD
- Redwood (Rishi): send evaluation agreement or accept PO once procurement confirms; include Deal ID DEAL-8421
- Jordan: schedule kickoff meeting for Monday 7/5 10am ET and share a calendar invite + Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAtlasPOC)

Attachments: redwood_poc_mop_v1.pdf (MOP), baseline_latency_samples.csv (schema)

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting started. If anything needs to shift on timing let me know and we’ll adapt.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
